title: A three-feature regression, measured three ways
prompt:
Fit a `LinearRegression` on body mass index, blood pressure and `s5` (the columns in `cols`) and measure it on the test set.

- `model`: the fitted regression.
- `pred`: its predictions for `X_test[cols]`.
- `mae`, `rmse`, `r2`: the three metrics from this lesson, computed on the test set.
hints: The metric functions take `(y_true, y_pred)` in that order.
explanation: Three well-chosen features get MAE about 42 and R² about 0.50, a slightly higher R² than all ten features reach on this split (0.49). That's common: a few features carry most of the signal, and extra correlated features add noise to the coefficients. RMSE is larger than MAE because a handful of patients are predicted badly, and squaring makes those misses count more.

checks.fitted: model is a fitted regression on three features
checks.mae: mae is the mean absolute error
checks.rmse: rmse is the root mean squared error
checks.r2: r2 is the test R² (and RMSE ≥ MAE)
